whatTheCourseTeaches: Dapp University selects a flash loan first (Balancer because its fee was zero, DODO as a fallback) and treats borrowed capital as the default for every arbitrage.

morpho-blue.label: Morpho Blue
morpho-blue.feeSource: Morpho Blue charges no flash-loan fee (no fee parameter exists on flashLoan); stated, not read from a getter

uniswap-v3-flash.label: Uniswap V3 pool flash / flash-swap
uniswap-v3-flash.feeModel: pool fee tier on the borrowed amount
uniswap-v3-flash.note: per-pool credit, not a single contract: cost is the pool fee tier on the borrowed amount, and capacity is that one pool
uniswap-v3-flash.feeBps: equal to the pool fee tier (e.g. 5 bps on a 0.05% pool)

affordability.method: For a borrowed notional N and a gross spread s (as a fraction of N), a flash loan at f bps is worth using only when s*N > f/10000*N + gas, i.e. the gross spread must exceed the flash-loan fee before gas is even counted.

breakEvenSpreadBps.uniswap-v3-flash: equal to the pool fee tier (e.g. 5 bps on a 0.05% pool)

affordability.note: A zero-fee provider (Balancer V2, Morpho Blue) imposes no spread threshold at all, so on Base the fee question is not what decides the funding method - the extra gas of the borrow/repay callback is.

aaveAt5bps.reading: Aave's 5 bps premium costs $5.00 on a $10,000 borrow. The median observed Base arbitrage nets $0.0187, so a borrow above roughly $37 notional would hand the entire median profit to the lender.
